title: Catch-all customer lookup that runs twice a minute
prompt: Support lookup screen: about 2 calls per minute. 80% of calls pass only @Email and return 0 to 3 rows; the others
pass @RegionID with @Tier. Every call takes about 1.9 s: the cached plan is a Clustered Index Scan of PK_Customers
(2.0M rows, about 31,000 logical reads) with the three OR predicates as a residual filter. Measured compile time is
3 ms. IX_Customers_Email and IX_Customers_RegionID exist. A call with all three parameters NULL is allowed and
returns every customer, including those with no email address.
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.

Customers: 2.0M rows. Tier S = 1.85M, G = ~150k, P = 25 partner accounts (CustomerID 1 to 25). IsActive = 1 for 88%. Email is NULL for ~9% (~180k rows, ~160k of them active). About 2% of non-NULL emails are shared by two or more customer rows (households). ReferredByCustomerID is non-NULL for 18%; 312 rows are self-referrals (ReferredByCustomerID = CustomerID, CustomerID 500001 to 500312). AccountNumber always matches 'AC' + 10 digits (CHECK constraint).

correct_families.description: At 2 calls per minute and 3 ms per compile, a fresh plan per call is cheap. The optimizer then removes the predicates whose parameter is NULL and seeks on the one that is given.
Build only the predicates that are supplied and run the text with sp_executesql and real parameters.
reference_sql: DECLARE @sql nvarchar(max) = N'SELECT c.CustomerID, c.AccountNumber, c.Email, c.Tier
IF @RegionID IS NOT NULL SET @sql += N' AND c.RegionID = @RegionID';
IF @Tier     IS NOT NULL SET @sql += N' AND c.Tier = @Tier';
IF @Email    IS NOT NULL SET @sql += N' AND c.Email = @Email';
EXEC sys.sp_executesql @sql, N'@RegionID tinyint, @Tier char(1), @Email varchar(254)', @RegionID, @Tier, @Email;

traps.why: c.Email = ISNULL(@Email, c.Email) is not an optional filter on a nullable column. With @Email NULL it is c.Email = c.Email, which drops every customer whose Email is NULL (about 9%).
traps.told_apart_by: Parameter case no_filter: the 180k customers with a NULL Email disappear.

traps.why: The email comes from a support agent's text box. Concatenating it into the statement allows SQL injection.
example_sql: DECLARE @sql nvarchar(max) = N'SELECT c.CustomerID, c.AccountNumber, c.Email, c.Tier
IF @RegionID IS NOT NULL SET @sql += N' AND c.RegionID = @RegionID';
IF @Tier     IS NOT NULL SET @sql += N' AND c.Tier = @Tier';
IF @Email    IS NOT NULL SET @sql += N' AND c.Email = ''' + @Email + N'''';
EXEC sys.sp_executesql @sql, N'@RegionID tinyint, @Tier char(1), @Email varchar(254)', @RegionID, @Tier, @Email;

traps.why: OPTIMIZE FOR UNKNOWN changes the estimates, not the shape: one plan must still be valid for every NULL combination, so it still scans.

min_improvement.basis: The scan reads about 31,000 pages. The dominant email path is a seek with a few lookups.

key.reference_notes: The same pattern at 40 calls per second needs dynamic SQL instead: see the task converted from rewrite exam Q02.
